You are a READ-ONLY code-quality reviewer. Do NOT edit any files. Review ONLY for the **Efficiency** angle. Do not hunt for correctness bugs.

## Scope
Code diff under review:
- `/tmp/simplify_main.diff` — main repo (driver/, include/, tests/, runtime/)
- `/tmp/simplify_sub.diff` — the `verilator/` git submodule (src/hybrid/, tests/hybrid/)
Repo root: `/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim`. Submodule at `/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/`.

## What the change does (context)
"L26 V-scratch reservation": the V-register transport scratch moved from a fixed guest address to the **top page of the shared mmap**; the driver maps one page above `--mem-size` (scheme D); plus a load-time ELF-overlap reject (`elf_load_top` in `driver/elf_syms.cpp`, checked in `driver/cmd_run.cpp`). New: `v_scratch_gpa()`, `physical_mmap_bytes()`/`max_program_mem_bytes()` (`driver/shm.cpp`), `kVScratchGpaUnset` guard + required-when-V ctor arg on `ResumeDriver`/`StateDrain`.
Note: `driver/state_diff.*` is from a PRIOR task (L24) — ignore unless egregious.

## Your angle: EFFICIENCY
Flag wasted work the diff INTRODUCES. Read the changed files for context. Specifically:
- `elf_load_top()` (`driver/elf_syms.cpp`) `slurp`s the ENTIRE ELF file into memory just to read the program-header table. Is this a new, redundant full-file read on the hybrid run's startup path? Note it does run once per `andes-sim run` (not a hot loop), but flag if it reads more than needed or if `elf_entry`/`resolve_pc`/`elf_load_top` now each slurp the same file separately on one run (repeated I/O of the same ELF).
- Any independent operations newly run sequentially that could be combined (e.g. multiple ELF passes).
- Long-lived objects built from closures/captured environments added by the diff (e.g. the `make_stream_sink` lambda in `simulator.hpp`, or controller construction) that keep a large enclosing scope alive — prefer a struct copying only needed fields. Check whether the diff's controller/`v_scratch_gpa()` plumbing introduced any such capture.
- Blocking work added to startup or a per-retire hot path (e.g. the `check_hybrid_handoff` retire loop in `simulator.hpp` — did the diff add per-retire cost?).

## Output
A list of findings. For each: `file:line`, one-line summary, concrete cost (what work is wasted/repeated), and the cheaper alternative. Distinguish "once per run" (low cost) from "per iteration/retire" (real). If already efficient, say so. Be conservative.

`driver/cmd_run.cpp:377` calls `elf_load_top(elf_path, e)`, and `driver/elf_syms.cpp:127-160` `slurp`s the entire ELF into a `std::vector<char>` just to walk the program-header table.

On one `andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger pc <elf>`, the same ELF file is now read from disk **three** times in immediate succession on the startup path:
- `driver/cmd_run.cpp:328` -> `hybrid_trigger` -> `resolve_pc` (pc-start) slurps once (`elf_syms.cpp:60`)
- same `hybrid_trigger` -> `resolve_pc` (pc-end) slurps a second time (`elf_syms.cpp:60`)
- `driver/cmd_run.cpp:377` -> `elf_load_top` slurps a third time (`elf_syms.cpp:130`)

(marker/icount mode: `resolve_pc` is not called, so `elf_load_top` is just 1 slurp — see `hybrid.cpp:13,31`.)

Concrete cost: pc-mode does 3 reads of the whole file where 1 would do. For the linked `rt_c_*` fixtures that is ~53 KiB read 3x (~159 KiB); asm fixtures ~5 KiB. This runs once per `andes-sim run`, not in any loop, so wall-clock impact is negligible (sub-millisecond, file is in page cache after the first read). `elf_load_top` itself reads the whole file but only needs the ELF header + program-header table — `slurp` is the existing shared primitive though, and every sibling (`elf_entry`, `resolve_pc`, `symbolize`) already slurps the whole file, so this is consistent with the file's established pattern, not a regression in approach.

Cheaper alternative (only if you want it): slurp the ELF once in `run_hybrid` and pass the buffer to header/symbol/load-top parsers — but that is a refactor of the whole `elf_syms` API (all four functions take a path and slurp), out of proportion to a once-per-run sub-ms cost.
